![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The calculation of `max_blocks_per_seq` here computes the **average** number of blocks per sequence, not the **maximum**. If any sequence in the batch has more pages than the average, the `prepare` kernel will silently truncate the block table for that sequence (see `csrc/fmha_v2_prepare.cu:60`), leading to incorrect attention results or out-of-bounds memory accesses in the subsequent attention kernel. 

Since the goal is to avoid D2H transfers of the indptr, you could use `len(paged_kv_indices)` as a safe (though potentially large) upper bound for the stride, or perform a two-pass approach where the first pass computes the actual maximum on the GPU.

feedback.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The calculation of `kv_len_i` does not correctly handle empty sequences (where `num_pages_i == 0`). If `num_pages_i` is 0, `max(num_pages_i - 1, 0)` is 0, so `kv_len_i` becomes `paged_kv_last_page_len[i]`. If `paged_kv_last_page_len` contains non-zero values for empty sequences (which is common if it's computed via a formula like `((len - 1) % page_size) + 1`), the sequence length will be reported incorrectly.

```
  int kv_len_i = (num_pages_i == 0) ? 0 : (num_pages_i - 1) * page_size + paged_kv_last_page_len[i];
```

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Fix out-of-bounds write risk in `max_blocks_per_seq` calculation.**

The current calculation `(len(paged_kv_indices) + batch_size - 1) // batch_size` computes the ceiling of the *average* pages per sequence, not the *maximum*. This will cause GPU kernel out-of-bounds writes when sequences have uneven page distributions (e.g., one sequence with 50 pages vs others with 5 pages each results in buffer size 2×28=56 pages total, insufficient for the 50-page sequence).

The CPU fallback at lines 2103–2105 correctly uses `max(blocks_per_seq)` by computing the difference between consecutive `paged_kv_indptr` values. The GPU path must do the same or use a conservative upper bound:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-                    max_blocks_per_seq = (
-                        len(paged_kv_indices) + batch_size - 1
-                    ) // max(batch_size, 1)
+                    # Conservative upper bound: max possible pages for any single sequence
+                    max_blocks_per_seq = len(paged_kv_indices)
```
</details>

Alternatively, have the GPU kernel compute and return the actual `max_blocks_per_seq` in a metadata tensor to avoid the conservative (but wasteful) upper bound.

feedback.body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The rounding logic for `exp` in the Python reference implementation does not handle non-finite inputs (Inf/NaN) or the saturation boundary at 254 consistently with the PTX implementation in `float_to_ue8m0_fast`. Specifically, if `exp` is `0xFF` (255), `round_up` will be true, making `exp` 256, which wraps to 0 when cast to `uint8`. The PTX implementation saturates all values above 254 to 254. Adding an explicit clamp will ensure bitwise exactness for extreme values.

```suggestion
    round_up = (mantissa > 0) & ~((exp == 0) & (mantissa <= 0x400000))
    exp = (exp + round_up.to(torch.int32)).clamp(0, 254)
```

feedback.author: gemini-code-assist[bot]
feedback.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces a W4A16 (BF16 activation, FP4 weight) fused MoE kernel path for Blackwell SM120/SM121 GPUs, complementing the existing NVFP4 (W4A4) path. It adds static, dynamic, and direct micro kernels for W4A16, along with a hybrid dispatch mechanism in `B12xMoEWrapper` to route prefill requests to CUTLASS and decode requests to the custom b12x kernels. Feedback on the changes highlights opportunities to improve robustness and maintainability, including replacing `.view()` with `.reshape()` to prevent runtime errors on non-contiguous tensors, logging warnings instead of silently swallowing exceptions in the CUDA capability check, and removing duplicated PTX/LLM assembly helpers in the new dynamic kernel by importing them from `fp4_common.py`.

<details>
<summary>I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.</summary>

### flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py (1271-1272)

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using `.view()` on `launch_ids` and `flat_weights` can raise a `RuntimeError` if the underlying tensors are not contiguous (for example, if `topk_ids` or `topk_weights` passed by the user were non-contiguous slices). It is highly recommended to use `.reshape(num_tokens, top_k)` instead of `.view(num_tokens, top_k)` to ensure robustness against non-contiguous inputs.

```suggestion
                topk_ids=launch_ids.reshape(num_tokens, top_k),
                topk_weights=flat_weights.reshape(num_tokens, top_k),
```

### flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py (1073-1116)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

In `_compiled_direct_micro_accepts_block_dim`, any unexpected exception during the CUDA library or attribute retrieval is silently caught and sets `accepted = False`. This silently disables the low-latency direct micro kernel and falls back to the static kernel without any indication to the user, which can make performance regressions extremely difficult to debug (e.g., if there is a metadata mismatch or a missing dependency). Consider logging a warning or using `warnings.warn` when an exception is caught.

### flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py (377-378)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Using `.view(torch.long)` on `w1_q` and `w2_q` assumes that the tensors are contiguous and their shapes are compatible. While you have added `.contiguous()`, if the tensor is not compatible or if there is a mismatch in the expected dimensions, `.view()` can raise a runtime error. It is safer to use `.reshape()` or explicitly validate the shape compatibility before performing the bitcast view.

### flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/moe_w4a16_dynamic_kernel.py (137-246)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

There is significant code duplication here where several PTX/LLM assembly helpers (such as `_st_shared_i32`, `_ld_shared_i32`, `_ld_global_acquire_i32`, `_st_global_release_i32`, `_spin_wait_global_eq_i32`, `_threadfence`, and `_atomic_cas_global_i32`) are redefined with a leading underscore. These are already defined in `flashinfer/cute_dsl/fp4_common.py` with proper type annotations and location tracking (`loc`, `ip`) passed to `llvm.inline_asm`. Please remove these duplicated definitions and import them directly from `flashinfer.cute_dsl.fp4_common`, just as is done in `moe_w4a16_static_kernel.py`.

</details>

feedback.author: qiching
feedback.body:
some nit on doc: call out the two real tradeoffs of enabling hybrid dispatch.

- Weight memory ~doubles. With cutlass_prefill_threshold > 0 the caller must keep both the b12x-format and the CUTLASS-format FP4 weights resident at the same time. For large MoE models this is a significant memory cost, please state it explicitly in the main class docstring (not just in register_cutlass_prefill_weights) so users can weigh it.
- CUDA graph captures a single path per shape. The b12x/CUTLASS branch is a host-side Python decision, so any captured graph freezes whichever path the token count selected at capture time. This is fine for per-shape-bucket graphs, but worth a one-line note in the docstring so users serving with CUDA graphs aren't surprised.

feedback.author: qiching
feedback.body:
i think the tests lack any numerical correctness checks:

all assertions only check shape, dtype, `isfinite`, and dispatch call counts and by my understanding, the core premise of the entire PR is that “b12x and Cutlass weights share FP4 numeric values,” but not a single test verifies whether the outputs of the two paths are consistent near the threshold. Assume there is any mismatch in the Cutlass prefill path regarding quantization or activation mapping, the tests will still fail even if they all show passed.

And , `_make_b12x_weights(seed=0)` and `_make_cutlass_weights(seed=1)` use completely independent random weights, so even if we wanted to perform cross check, we couldn’t. So my recommendation is we can use the same BF16 baseline to generate both layouts simultaneously, and add a `test_hybrid_matches_pure_b12x` test, and compare the hybrid output with the pure B12X output at `m == threshold`.

_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`Is CUTLASS grouped GEMM / fused MoE kernel execution deterministic (bit-exact) across repeated launches with identical inputs on the same GPU?`

💡 Result:

CUTLASS grouped GEMM and fused MoE kernels are not inherently guaranteed to be deterministic (bit-exact) across repeated launches, as their determinism depends on the specific kernel configuration, scheduling strategy, and hardware architecture [1][2][3]. Key factors influencing determinism include: 1. Kernel Schedulers and Strategies: While standard data-parallel kernels may be deterministic, advanced scheduling techniques like Stream-K introduce mechanisms that can impact bit-exactness [2][3]. For instance, Stream-K tile schedulers offer different reduction strategies: - Non-deterministic: Uses atomic aggregation, which is generally faster but leads to non-deterministic results due to the non-associative nature of floating-point operations [4][3]. - Deterministic/Mixed: Employs strategies such as turnstile-ordered atomic aggregation or separate reduction waves to ensure bit-exact results, albeit often at a performance cost [2][3]. 2. Floating-Point Non-Associativity: Because floating-point addition is not associative—meaning (a + b) + c does not necessarily equal a + (b + c)—any kernel that changes the order of accumulation across different launches (e.g., due to dynamic work scheduling or variations in GPU occupancy) will produce non-bit-exact results [4]. 3. MoE Specifics: Fused MoE kernels often utilize these underlying CUTLASS primitives [5][6]. Efforts to achieve "batch invariance" or determinism in MoE kernels require enforcing specific configurations, such as using persistent tile schedulers and cooperative schedules, and avoiding non-deterministic reduction paths [1]. In practice, developers requiring bit-exactness must explicitly configure kernels to use deterministic modes where available and verify their specific use case, as standard benchmarks or default configurations may prioritize performance over bit-exact determinism [1][2]. Verification is typically handled through unit tests that compare results against a reference implementation using epsilon-based relative equality rather than strict bit-comparison for floating-point outputs [7][4][8].

feedback.body:
Good catch — addressed in 36d4d9c with one tightening and one deferral. Splitting the comment in two:

**On the partial MIS input → invalid memory:** agreed. The new commit adds a symmetric `assert` in *both* `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.run` (line ~2384) and the new `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper.run` requiring `_token_pos_in_items_ptr` *and* `_max_item_len_ptr` to be non-None whenever `_prefix_len_ptr` is. The paged wrapper has had the same single-pointer check since MIS was first introduced, so the hardening is symmetric. In current callers (sglang's `MultiItemScoringParams`) all three are set as a tuple in `plan()` so this is defense-in-depth, but the failure mode you describe would have been ugly otherwise.

**On the CUSTOM → MIS silent override:** the current order (`if custom_mask: mask_mode = CUSTOM` then `if prefix_len_ptr: mask_mode = MULTIITEMSCORING`) is the existing behavior of the paged wrapper too — MIS has implicit precedence today. The new ragged code mirrors that intentionally. Flipping the override to an error-on-conflict (or making them mutually exclusive at `plan()` time) is a real API contract change that should:
- touch *both* wrappers symmetrically,
- ideally be enforced earlier in `plan()` rather than at `run()` time so the failure is visible during setup,
- come with a separate test.

Happy to follow up with a dedicated PR if you'd prefer that direction. Existing callers I'm aware of (sglang `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.call_begin_forward`) already set `custom_mask=None` explicitly when MIS is active, so the override is currently dead code in practice — but the API contract is still worth nailing down.

This support check is leaking too much backend-resolution detail into `resolve_moe_cls()`. `resolve_moe_cls()` should only resolve the backend class; the MoE-LoRA support policy and error formatting should live in `check_moe_lora_supported()`.

Could we pass the resolved `moe_cls` and the originally requested backend name into `check_moe_lora_supported()` instead? That keeps the exact-Cutlass-kernel rule centralized with the quant/backend support matrix, and avoids callers needing to synthesize a `resolved_backend`string.



```python
  # tensorrt_llm/_torch/modules/fused_moe/create_moe.py

  if (moe_cls == TRTLLMGenFusedMoE and not has_quant
          and not
  TRTLLMGenFusedMoE._supports_flashinfer_bf16_routing_method(
              routing_method)):
      moe_cls = CutlassFusedMoE

  check_moe_lora_supported(
      moe_cls=moe_cls,
      requested_moe_backend=model_config.moe_backend,
      lora_config=model_config.lora_config,
      quant_config=effective_quant_config,
      layer_idx=layer_idx,
  )

  return moe_cls
```

Line 4438 currently treats every full `uniqueTokens` block as commit-ready, but this file consistently uses `getUsableUniqueTokenCountForReuse(...)` to exclude the unmaterialized tail token and to respect chunked prefill progress. +    auto const numFullTokenBlocks = usableUniqueTokenCount / tokensPerBlock;

feedback.author: NVShreyas
feedback.body:
yes we have checks for heads and seq len divisibility in SequenceSharder - 
```
if seq_len % self._size != 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sequence length ({seq_len}) along dim {dim} is not "
                f"divisible by SequenceSharder.size ({self._size}). "
                f"Pass pad_to_multiple=True or adjust input dimensions."
            )
```
for cross-attention specifically, hidden states or encoder states need to be sharded and go through this path ensuring that seq lens are divisible.
I will remove this redundant check

feedback.author: okorzh-amd
feedback.body: Good catch, you're right, that expansion is unnecessary and I've reverted it. The assert was hit but only before the get_cudagraph_support change. The original ROCm CI failure was exactly this bare assert m.max_query_len <= self.reorder_batch_threshold firing (with no message, which is what made it hard to diagnose) when a SINGLE_ONLY MLA backend (TRITON_MLA) was used with spec decode under FULL_AND_PIECEWISE. I originally expanded it into an actionable ValueError while still tracking down the root cause.

feedback.author: okorzh-amd
feedback.body:
The actual problem is exactly what you said: the child class advertises something it can't do. TritonMLAMetadataBuilder declared _cudagraph_support = UNIFORM_BATCH but inherits query_len_support = SINGLE_ONLY. Per the enum docs, UNIFORM_BATCH means "can be used for spec-decode" (multi-token uniform), so that's an incorrect claim for a single-token-only backend. CutlassMLAMetadataBuilder (also SINGLE_ONLY) already gets this right — it declares UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE ("enable full CUDA Graph support for decode-only capture"). So I just made TritonMLA match:
```
_cudagraph_support: ClassVar[AttentionCGSupport] = (
    AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE
)
```
Still captures decode-only full graphs (no regression for single-token), and lets the dispatcher downgrade FULL → PIECEWISE under spec decode. I confirmed this isn't hiding a broader issue: TritonMLA is the only MLACommonMetadataBuilder subclass that declared UNIFORM_BATCH while inheriting SINGLE_ONLY — every other UNIFORM_BATCH MLA builder sets query_len_support to UNIFORM/VARLEN, and the sparse builders subclass AttentionMetadataBuilder directly (no query_len_support).

I've reverted the get_cudagraph_support override, so mla_attention.py is now identical to upstream.

feedback.author: tomeras91
feedback.body:
This is still accepting a str of comma-separated ints. It's just a redundant complication.
`delay_iterations` can be just a list of ints:
```python
delay_iterations: list[int] = Field(default_factory=lambda: [0])
```

With that, you don't need all the logic in `_parse_iteration_values` - passing multiple values in the CLI will automatically parse into a list of ints (uses `nargs="+"` in the arg parser - see `collection_to_kwargs` in `arg_utils.py`). So, the CLI line:
```bash
--profiler-config.delay_iterations 10 100
```
or, equivalently
```bash
    --profiler-config '{"profiler":"cuda",
                        "delay_iterations":[10,100],
                        "max_iterations":[20,100]}'
```
Will just be parsed to `delay_iterations=[10,100]` in this class. 

Furthermore, you can even use:
```python
delay_iterations: list[Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)]] = Field(default_factory=lambda: [0])
```
And then you gat the `>=0` validation natively from pydantic (and you can delete that logic from `_validate_profiler_config`.

To handle the single window case (and auto-parse to a single-element list), you can add a "before" field validator:
```python
@field_validator("delay_iterations", mode="before")
@classmethod
def _wrap_scalar(cls, v):
    return [v] if isinstance(v, int) else v

@field_validator("max_iterations", mode="before")
@classmethod
def _validate_max_iterations(cls, v):
    v = [v] if isinstance(v, int) else v
    # here you can also add the "max_iterations can be 0 only for the final window logic". It belongs here and not in `_validate_multi_window_config` which should just check things that are a property of the window and not the delay/max values themselves.
    return v
```

>Hey @tlrmchlsmth, thanks for the PR. Did you happen to test with FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4 backend? On my end I see garbage output with Flashinfer backend. 

I didn't try it, sorry

>After some digging, Flashinfer kernels currently don't support page/block stride layout and only calculates token strides. As a result, the packing here would corrupt attention. Do you think we should gate this packing when using the Flashinfer backedn?

This sounds plausible. Do you have any breadcrumbs you can point to? Would definitely make sense to gate this and also raise it with the FlashInfer team

feedback.author: majunze2001
feedback.body: Issue opened here with minimal reproduction commands: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47783. I've also opened a feature request in flashinfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3856
